note: Community-curated, no-root-first. Every entry lists an explicit access requirement. Descriptions are paraphrased; links point at the upstream project.

sections.name: Start here — the no-root foundation
sections.blurb: Without one of these two, nothing else in the list can touch system settings.

entries.name: Shizuku
entries.description: The keystone of the whole no-root ecosystem: starts a privileged shell over wireless debugging or ADB, then lends that access to apps you approve. Every Shizuku-based tool below depends on it.

entries.name: Android Platform Tools (adb)
entries.description: Official Google ADB binaries. Needed exactly once to bootstrap Shizuku or to run this toolkit's generated command sets from a computer.

entries.name: LADB
entries.description: A local ADB shell that talks to itself over wireless debugging. Handy escape hatch when a Shizuku session dies and you have no computer nearby.

entries.name: Termux
entries.description: Full Linux userland on the phone. Pair it with the ADB connection trick and you can script your own tweaks from the device itself.

sections.name: FPS, refresh rate & gaming
sections.blurb: The category this toolkit was born in. OriginOS's high-refresh whitelist is the thing everyone fights.

entries.name: VivoIQOO144FPSUnlocker
entries.description: Purpose-built for Vivo/iQOO on OriginOS: forces 144 Hz in apps that are not on the high-refresh whitelist, with a built-in FPS counter. It has an APK mirror listing, which is why it went viral on TikTok in the iQOO community.

entries.name: otweak
entries.description: Indie Kotlin/ADB project for Android customisation with a system-level tweaking bent. Small, active, worth reading for how it layers ADB commands into a UI.

entries.name: FrameX
entries.description: Overlay with a live FPS meter and thermal diagnostics, driving optimisation through Shizuku. Explicitly targets Vivo OriginOS/FuntouchOS builds.

entries.name: Game Booster / FPS Unlocker
entries.description: Game FPS unlocking and device profiling: resolution scaling, an FPS/CPU/RAM/temperature overlay, crosshair overlay and a DNS optimiser. Shizuku for no-root use, LSPosed if you are rooted.

entries.name: Android Game Booster
entries.description: Universal resolution scaler with a one-time ADB setup for non-rooted devices. Claims large frame-rate gains on GPU-bound titles.

entries.name: SystemUI Tuner
entries.description: Long-standing tool for hiding status-bar icons, tuning immersive mode and unlocking flags the OEM hides. Overlaps with this toolkit's display section and does it with more polish.

sections.name: Optimisation & tuning
sections.blurb: Profiles, schedulers and kernel-ish tuning with varying degrees of honesty about what a no-root device can do.

entries.name: NRAO — Non-Root Android Optimizer
entries.description: Optimiser that works purely with shell-accessible knobs, no root required. Exactly what the name says.

entries.name: ADB Android Optimizer
entries.description: Ships power-saving, balanced and max-hardware profiles as ADB command sets, with Shizuku/Shizushell support so you only need a PC for the first setup.

entries.name: Android battery optimization
entries.description: Focused ADB recipes that maximise battery life and screen-on time on a stock, non-rooted device without deep system modification.

entries.name: AndroidTweaker
entries.description: Universal Magisk module that balances kernel and RAM behaviour with configurable profiles and no terminal work. Listed for reference — it is the rooted counterpart to what this toolkit does.

entries.name: CoreTaskOptimizer
entries.description: CPU affinity, scheduler priority and I/O policy management that detects performance versus efficiency cores at runtime. Root-only, but the detection logic is worth studying.

entries.name: KTweak
entries.description: The most-referenced kernel tuning script in the Android community. Included as the canonical reference for what root buys you — and what this toolkit deliberately cannot do.

sections.name: Debloat & app management
sections.blurb: Disable what you do not want without touching a system partition.

entries.name: Universal Android Debloater
entries.description: Cross-platform Rust GUI that debloats over ADB. Improves privacy, security and battery, and is designed so that you cannot brick the device.

entries.name: Universal Android Debloater NG
entries.description: The maintained next-generation rewrite of the debloater. Better multi-user support and a cleaner package database.

entries.name: App Manager
entries.description: The Swiss-army knife for package introspection: permissions, trackers, activities, app ops, and ADB-mode freeze/uninstall. Does more than this toolkit ever will, with a steeper learning curve.

entries.name: Hail
entries.description: Freeze, unfreeze and hibernate apps through Shizuku or root. The cleanest way to make bloatware inert without uninstalling anything.

entries.name: Canta
entries.description: Single-purpose Shizuku debloater with a curated list of packages that are safe to remove per vendor — including Vivo entries.

entries.name: Obtainium
entries.description: Installs and updates apps straight from GitHub, F-Droid and other sources. The practical way to keep all the sideloaded tools in this list current.

entries.name: SAI — Split APKs Installer
entries.description: Installs split APK bundles (XAPK/APKS) without root or a PC. Most modern phone APKs you find online are split, and the system installer will refuse them.

sections.name: Privacy, firewall & tracking
sections.blurb: Who is talking to your phone, and how to stop the boring half of it.

entries.name: NetGuard
entries.description: No-root firewall that blocks network access per app through the local VPN slot. The single most effective privacy tool you can install without root.

entries.name: TrackerControl
entries.description: Shows which trackers each app contacts and lets you block them individually. Excellent companion to a debloat session for understanding what you just disabled.

entries.name: εxodus
entries.description: Reports the trackers embedded in any installed app, using the Exodus Privacy static-analysis database.

entries.name: Intra
entries.description: Encrypted-DNS client from Jigsaw. A UI-first alternative to this toolkit's Private DNS tweak if you prefer a per-app, switchable setup.

entries.name: awesome-shizuku
entries.description: The canonical curated index of Shizuku-powered apps: debloat, audio, display, automation and more. If an app in our list has a better alternative, it is probably on that page.

entries.name: best Shizuku apps for no-root
entries.description: Another community index of Shizuku and wireless-ADB tools, with a heavier emphasis on automation and customisation.

sections.name: Display, launcher & audio
sections.blurb: The parts of customisation that never needed root in the first place.

entries.name: Wavelet
entries.description: System-wide audio effects headphone profile, bass boost and auto-EQ, built on the official DynamicsProcessing API. No root, no audio HAL patching.

entries.name: RootlessJamesDSP
entries.description: JamesDSP's convolution and bass processing without root, using the audio playback capture API. The most capable no-root DSP available.

entries.name: Lawnchair
entries.description: AOSP-based launcher that brings a Pixel-like (or entirely your own) home screen to OriginOS, which is often the single biggest visual upgrade available.

entries.name: scrcpy
entries.description: Low-latency screen mirroring and control over ADB, no root and no app installed on the phone. Essential for testing tweaks without picking the device up.

entries.name: DSU Sideloader
entries.description: Boots a GSI or a second Android image through Dynamic System Updates without erasing your data. The safest way to try a different ROM before committing.
